learn.title: Two triangles worth knowing
learn.body: Two right triangles show up constantly, and their side ratios are fixed. If you know the ratio, you can find sides without using the theorem each time.

learn.title: The 45-45-90 triangle
learn.body: Half of a square cut along its diagonal. The two legs are equal and the angles are $45^\circ,45^\circ,90^\circ$. If each leg is $s$, the hypotenuse is $s\sqrt{2}$. The sides are in the ratio $1:1:\sqrt{2}$.

learn.title: The 30-60-90 triangle
learn.body: Half of an equilateral triangle cut down the middle. If the short leg (opposite $30^\circ$) is $s$, the hypotenuse is $2s$ and the long leg (opposite $60^\circ$) is $s\sqrt{3}$. The ratio is $1:\sqrt{3}:2$.

learn.title: Use the ratios
steps: A 45-45-90 triangle has hypotenuse $8\sqrt{2}$. Each leg is 8.
A 30-60-90 triangle has short leg 6. Hypotenuse $=12$.

learn.body: Check with the theorem: legs 1 and $\sqrt{3}$ give $1+3=4$, and the hypotenuse is $\sqrt{4}=2$. The ratio is right.

questions.prompt: A 45-45-90 triangle has legs of length 5. What is the hypotenuse?
questions.explanation: The hypotenuse is a leg times $\sqrt{2}$.

questions.prompt: The short leg of a 30-60-90 triangle is 6. Find the hypotenuse.
questions.explanation: The hypotenuse is twice the short leg.

questions.prompt: The short leg of a 30-60-90 triangle is 4. What is the long leg?
questions.explanation: The long leg is the short leg times $\sqrt{3}$.

questions.prompt: The hypotenuse of a 45-45-90 triangle is $8\sqrt{2}$. Find the length of each leg.
questions.explanation: Hypotenuse $=$ leg $\times\sqrt{2}$, so the leg is 8.

questions.prompt: In a 30-60-90 triangle the hypotenuse is \_\_ times the short leg.
questions.explanation: The sides are in the ratio $1:\sqrt{3}:2$.

questions.prompt: The hypotenuse of a 30-60-90 triangle is 20. What is the short leg?
questions.explanation: The short leg is half of the hypotenuse.

questions.prompt: Match each triangle to its side ratio.
pairs: A right triangle with whole sides
questions.explanation: The two special triangles have fixed ratios because they are halves of a square and an equilateral triangle.
